findings.text: blocking: the solved magnetic axis is read by polishing one seed through a flat, multi-modal flux core, so axis_offset_cm is not a determined quantity; on head frame 137 the spline has four in-plasma qualified maxima within 1.7 mWb of each other at (1.5440,-0.2703), (1.5768,-0.1957), (1.5462,+0.2803) and (1.5839,+0.1972), giving axis Z offsets of -27.20, -19.74, +27.86 and +19.55 cm, and on 146 four maxima give -22.62, -5.71, -8.34 and +2.39 cm; the fragment's sentence "The axes move down 27.20 cm and 22.62 cm" therefore reports which basin the stored seed falls in, not a measured displacement, and the same record's robust current centroids sit 26.6 cm and 21.3 cm above the reported axis while essentially matching EFIT's Z.

non-blocking: stationary duplicates the capability already owned by scripts/diiid_map_fidelity/measure.py:143 polish, including the same RectBivariateSpline root and the same gradient and Hessian-determinant qualification, without calling, wrapping or extending the owner; scripts/prototypes/diiid_axis_identification/census.py:64 also already enumerates every critical point, which is the check that would have exposed the degenerate core.

non-blocking: the only axis test polishes a well-conditioned synthetic field seeded exactly on its axis, so nothing fails if a real map's axis is ambiguous or if analyze() picks a different basin; an end-to-end assertion on one committed bank with a checked axis count would guard the number the record turns on.

non-blocking: the measurement log's revision line names feead21e8, a commit that does not contain scripts/prototypes/diiid_xpoint_offset/decompose.py, and negative-control.log:1 carries the same revision although its run post-dates that commit, so neither header identifies the code that produced its numbers; after-suite.log correctly names 4082789df.

round_answers.current_and_force_reads: current_and_force at decompose.py:186-225 does what it claims: j_phi from nova.equilibrium.map_extraction.apply_delta_star (the Ampere/Grad-Shafranov stencil, -Delta-star Phi/(2 pi mu0 R)) integrated as j*dR*dZ, and F_R=+sum 2 pi R j B_Z, F_Z=-sum 2 pi R j B_R, which is the correct e_phi x B_p cross product; the analytic test at tests/test_xpoint_offset_decomposition.py:74-102 pins both sign and magnitude. Own-field only, no pressure term, and the differing solved/reference supports are stated in the fragment.
round_answers.numbers_vs_receipt_and_panels: All values in the fragment reconcile with results.json head rows. The panels draw the axis markers at the record's own offsets: pixel geometry of figure-previews-4082789df/frame-137-diverted.png, calibrated on the two EFIT markers, gives 160.6 px/m and a solved-minus-EFIT axis separation of (-17.6, -26.6) cm against the recorded (-17.91, -27.20) cm. The 'few cm' the contours show is the contour-loop centre, not the flux maximum: the solved core is flat to about 0.1 percent, so the innermost loop is centred ~10 cm inboard of EFIT while the polished maximum sits 27 cm below it. Both readings are faithful to the panel; the axis they describe is not a determined quantity.
round_answers.recommendation: It follows from the evidence as a next step: nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py:3545 is the source current_moments evaluation the fragment cites, :3962 composes external plus plasma flux, and :3661 normalises total current but not centroid, so a branch-dependent current shape is a live hypothesis the record labels as such. The caveat is that the axis should not be used to judge the next state until it is well-conditioned.
round_answers.verdict_and_threshold: The rigid/local rule at decompose.py:109-126 is applied as stated and its limitation is disclosed in the fragment (the converged MAST base control is classed local). The local verdict for 137D and 146D survives the axis ambiguity: using the alternative qualified maxima, the axis-to-X vector difference still exceeds the 50 percent coherence bound on both frames.
